channel.title: KhingPaste
channel.description: Update feed for KhingPaste, the macOS clipboard history app.

item.description:
A new look: KhingPaste now wears the same glass as KhingShot and Quorum.

In the history

  • See the whole copy before you paste it. A preview beside the list shows

the full text, the link, the command, the color, the picture, or the file and where it came from, with its length, formats, and when you first copied it.

  • Rows show what you copied. Colors show their swatch, images their

thumbnail, commands read in monospace, and links lead with the site.

  • History and Pinned are tabs. Your pinned copies get their own page, kept

past the size limit as before.

  • Filter by kind from the search field. Text, links, images, files,

commands, or colors, with a count for each. Matches are highlighted as you type.

  • Clear History shows what goes and what stays before you confirm, and

keeps your pinned copies unless you choose to take everything.

Everywhere else

  • A menu bar panel with your five newest copies, a switch to pause

recording, and the shortcut that opens the history.

  • Settings in pages: General, Shortcut, Permissions, History, and Updates.

Permissions says exactly what is missing and takes you to the right switch.

  • A short setup guide on first launch. If you are updating, you will not

see it.

Escape now closes the kind menu first, then clears your search, then closes the panel.

KhingPaste never checks a copied file on its own inside Desktop, Documents, or Downloads, so opening the history can never set off a macOS folder-access prompt over the app you are typing in. It checks when you open, reveal, or paste the file, as before.

Right-click any row, and updates now look like the rest of KhingSuite.

New

  • A context menu on every row. Right-click to paste, pin, preview, or delete

without reaching for a shortcut. Pinning and deleting used to be reachable only by keyboard, so a hand already on the mouse had no way to them at all.

  • Open and Reveal in Finder on a copied file. Copy a file, then send it

straight to Finder or open it, without pasting it anywhere first.

  • The update panel wears KhingSuite's own colours, the same one KhingShot

shows, rather than Sparkle's stock window.

The menu acts on the row you clicked rather than the selected one, so it never moves your place in the list.

A copied file is a path rather than a copy of the file itself, so it can be renamed, moved, or thrown away long before the row ages out of the history. KhingPaste checks before it acts, and says so in the panel instead of appearing to do nothing. If you copied several files and only some are still there, it opens the ones that are.

Press Space to see the image you are about to paste.

New

  • Preview an image on Space, the way Finder does. Select an image in the

history and press Space to open it full size across the panel. Tap the key and the preview stays up; hold it and the preview goes away when you let go. Both gestures work exactly as they do in Finder.

  • While a preview is open the arrow keys step between your images and swap the

picture in place, so you can flick through a run of screenshots without closing anything. Return still pastes the one you are looking at, and Escape or Space closes the preview.

A row showed an image as a 34-pixel thumbnail titled *Image 1920 x 1080*, which tells two screenshots taken a minute apart apart not at all. Now you can look before you paste.

The preview is drawn inside KhingPaste's own panel rather than handed to Quick Look, because Quick Look takes keyboard focus and KhingPaste's whole trick is never taking it from the app you were typing in.

Return now tells you when it can only copy.

Fixed

  • Pressing Return did nothing visible in some cases. With *Paste

automatically* switched on but Accessibility access missing, KhingPaste put the item on the clipboard and stopped there, with nothing on screen to say why. The panel now says so, and offers a Grant Access button that takes you straight to the right place in System Settings.

  • Access is re-checked every time the panel opens, so granting it takes effect

on your next paste rather than after a restart.

macOS drops Accessibility access whenever an app is replaced by a build signed differently, which is easy to hit and gives no warning. If Return has been copying rather than pasting, this release will tell you, and one click fixes it.

The first release that arrives through the updater rather than as a download.

New

  • The menu bar dropdown now shows which version you are on. KhingPaste has no

Dock icon and no About window, so until now the only way to find out was to open Settings and scroll to the bottom.

KhingPaste can now update itself.

New

  • Updates arrive in the app. KhingPaste checks once a day in the background

and offers the new version when there is one. Check for Updates… is in the menu bar, and Settings → Updates shows the running version, when it last checked, and a switch for the daily check.

  • A scheduled check never interrupts a history panel you have open. One you ask

for always runs.

Changed

  • KhingPaste now ships as a signed, notarised disk image rather than a zip.

Drag it to Applications the usual way.

  • Universal build: Apple silicon and Intel in one download.
